pw_striking_hall.name: The Old Mint — Striking-Hall
pw_striking_hall.desc: Hammer-frames stand in a long silent row, each cocked mid-stroke and never finished, coin-blanks still racked beside them waiting on a hand that will not come. On quarter-days, Pennywell swears, you can hear them anyway.
pw_striking_hall.brief: A row of silent hammer-frames, cocked mid-stroke.
onEnterOnce: This is the Old Vault's outer hall: the moneyers carried the king's coin and dies down past here, and the Reeve's men mortared the door behind them. Four hundred years on, the hammers still keep quarter-days.
Tamsin: "Listen — nothing's swinging, and that race outside hasn't turned in longer than the wheel's been broken. Whoever built these frames meant them to outlast the men working them. They have."

variants.desc: Hammer-frames stand in their long row, cocked still — but the air has lost the waiting feel it had. Whatever they were held ready for, it came once, and answered.
variants.brief: The frames, cocked still, but no longer waiting.

variants.desc: The hammer-frames stand scorched and warped, cinder-oil smoke still ghosting off the timber. Whatever quarter-day sound Pennywell used to hear, nobody's claimed to hear it since.
variants.brief: The frames, scorched; the old sound gone quiet.

pw_outer_strongroom.name: The Outer Strong-Room
pw_outer_strongroom.desc: A stone room short of the vault-door proper, shelves collapsed along one wall since the night the door went up. Whatever was being carried in a hurry that night, some of it never made the last few steps.
pw_outer_strongroom.brief: A stone room; shelves collapsed since the sealing.

actions.label: search where the shelves fell (wits)
fx: Wedged behind a fallen shelf, dropped and never missed in the hurry of that night: the mint's own obverse die, the first Reeve's face still cut sharp into its face.
Forty years of undisturbed dust and broken shelving, nothing more obvious than that. It can be searched again.

pw_vault_door.name: The Vault-Door
pw_vault_door.desc: Mortared stone where a door used to be, fitted so tight by the Reeve's own masons that not even damp gets through. The stone is warm, though — faintly, steadily, the way a hearth-wall stays warm long after the fire's out.
pw_vault_door.brief: Mortared stone, warm to the touch; no fire behind it.

in.lockedMsg: The door is mortared stone, whole. Nothing short of fire is getting through it.

variants.desc: Mortared stone, whole still — but the warmth in it has settled into something gentler, less like a held breath and more like a hearth banked for the night.
variants.brief: The mortared door, warm still, but settled now.

variants.desc: Mortared stone, whole, and Pennywell means to keep it that way. The warmth hasn't left it. Nobody who's felt it seems to want it to.
variants.brief: The mortared door, kept whole, and warm, by choice.

variants.desc: A ragged black gap where mortared stone used to be, cinder-oil scored deep into what's left of the frame. Whatever kept the stone warm went out with the door.
variants.brief: A burned-through gap; the warmth is gone.

actions.label: weigh what this grief asks
fx: The rite wants the king's penny struck once more at this door: both dies, and the three moneyers' names spoken.

But the moneyers won't strike, dies and names or not, while the Shieldings' dead still hold their line — cut the same night as this door, and it wants answering first: rest it, bargain it, or burn it, at Harrowfield.
The Shieldings have their answer now, one way or another. That excuse is gone from Pennywell's mouth.
The reverse die is still wanted: Sarel keeps it, at the Hammer Hearth — given, taken, or found.
The obverse die is still wanted: in the outer strong-room, from Slade's scrap, or washed up on the gravel spit.
All three moneyers' names are known: Doran's record, Meva's ledger, and the child's river penny read.
One name is missing still: Doran's record, at the assayer's cot.
One name is missing still: Meva's ledger of faces, at the tithe-house.
One name is missing still: read Robin's river penny, in the mint yard.
Everything's ready together: strike the king's penny once more, here at the door.
The bargain stands ready: tell Averil, at the counting-house, the vault stays sealed.
The bargain wants three refused, in Pennywell: the warden's warrant, the paymaster's chest, and the smelter's melt.
The burn stands ready: cinder-oil is yours — burn through the door here (might; a failed try costs 1 hp).
The burn wants cinder-oil — Slade, at the furnace-yard, gives it gladly.

actions.label: strike the penny (might, 1hp fail)
fx: You set both dies true and swing once, saying Corbet, Wyle, and Hann into the strike. The coin comes out whole, the first struck true in four hundred years — and from behind the stone, once, the hammers answer it.
Vell: "There. My own line's face, and theirs, on the same small piece of silver. I did not think that would ever sit easily in one hand. It very nearly does."
Tamsin: "That's a craftsman's answer, not a priest's. Dies, a die-hand, and a true swing. I'll allow it counts as a rite anyway."
The hammer skips its mark. The coin comes out bent, unspendable, unspeakable — and the names go unsaid for it. It can be tried again.

actions.label: burn the vault-door (might, 1hp fail)
fx: The cinder-oil eats through four hundred years of mortar in a night. By morning the door's a black gap, and whatever the moneyers were guarding is only silver again — melted, mostly, and easy now to claim.
Tamsin: "Quick, clean, and the forges eat well tonight. I won't pretend I'm sorry for it."
Vell: "My own family's coin, my own family's fire. I keep thinking someone should have asked those men first. Nobody did, either time."
The oil catches wrong on the damp stone and flares back short. You're driven off a step, singed, the door untouched.

pw_vault.name: The Vault
pw_vault.desc: The vault proper, walls scorched black where the cinder-oil ate through stone meant to last forever. Four moneyers lie where they sat down to wait, dies and coin-dust scattered around them like a trade left mid-count.
pw_vault.brief: The scorched vault; four moneyers, a trade left mid-count.

actions.label: search the scorched hoard
fx: Most of the hoard is a single fused lump now, faces melted past reading. You take what's still worth taking, and try not to look too long at the four of them.

pw_coin_blank.name: an unstruck coin-blank
pw_coin_blank.hint: blank on both faces; four hundred years of nobody deciding what to stamp on it

pw_reverse_die.name: the king's reverse die
pw_reverse_die.hint: wants the obverse to be struck true; Hann's own hand cut this one

variants.hint: struck true at the vault door; Sarel will want to know where it rests
the vault kept; the press strikes the old face from its own dies now — a keepsake
the vault burned through; nothing left to strike — a keepsake

pw_obverse_die.name: the king's obverse die
pw_obverse_die.hint: silver-black with age; the old king's face still sharp on it

variants.hint: struck true at the vault door; Sarel will want to know where it rests
the vault kept; the press strikes the old face from its own dies now — a keepsake
the vault burned through; nothing left to strike — a keepsake

pw_cinder_oil.name: a cask of Ironbound cinder-oil
pw_cinder_oil.hint: eats through mortar the way it eats through anything else old and stubborn

pw_hoard_silver.name: a fused lump of coin-silver, faces melted past reading
pw_hoard_silver.hint: coin melted past any face you'd know; worth is the silver alone now.

stages.text: The reverse die is yours. The obverse waits in the outer strong-room, in Slade's scrap, or on the gravel spit.
The obverse die is yours. The reverse waits with Sarel, at the Hammer Hearth — given, taken, or found.
Two dies are wanted: the reverse from Sarel, the obverse from the strong-room, the scrap, or the spit.
Two names are known: Doran's and Meva's. The last is Robin's river penny, read, in the mint yard.
Two names are known: Doran's and the river penny's. The last waits in Meva's ledger, at the tithe-house.
Two names are known: Meva's and the river penny's. The last waits in Doran's record, at the assayer's cot.
One name is known: Doran's record. Two remain: Meva's ledger and Robin's river penny.
One name is known: Meva's ledger. Two remain: Doran's record and Robin's river penny.
One name is known: the river penny's. Two remain: Doran's record and Meva's ledger.
Three names are wanted: Doran's record, Meva's ledger, and Robin's river penny, read.
Robin's river penny still hears hammers. Read it for a name, give it to Meva's ledger, or tell her to keep it unread.
Pennywell strikes the Crown's face now, the first Reeve's own, from the counting-house.
Pennywell's silver runs faceless now, weighed and not counted, out of the paymaster's chest-room.
Pennywell strikes the old king's face now, an Envoy's bargain the warden and the paymaster both signed.
Pennywell strikes the old king's face now, the Keepers' answer, settled at the assayer's cot or by the bargain itself.
The vault's fate is settled. Pennywell's coin is still open: the counting-house, the chest-room, or the assayer's cot.
Whose face Pennywell strikes waits on the vault's own fate being settled first.
The ford's safe line is known. Carry Dray's chest across it, at dusk.
Dray's chest wants carrying over the ford at dusk. Read the ford's line before you cross it.
The bargain's come due. Averil, at the counting-house, has news you won't like.
The rite is settled. Sarel, at the Hammer Hearth, wonders what becomes of the dies now.
The vault is ash and melt. Slade, at the furnace-yard, wants to know where the silver goes.
Pennywell settles back into itself, whatever the Old Vault's fate cost it.

epilogue.text: The king's penny was struck once more at Pennywell's vault-door, and the hammers under the ground answered it, once, and stopped.
Pennywell struck true only once Harrowfield's own truce was finally called — the same night's two debts, closed within one season.
Pennywell struck its penny only once the Shieldings' account was closed, one way or another. The moneyers never say aloud they were waiting.
Pennywell's vault stays sealed and warm, and its mint strikes an old king's face now, by nobody's leave but its own.
Ironbound cinder-oil ate through four hundred years of mortar in a night, and Pennywell's hoard went into the forges by morning.
Pennywell's vault stands mortared still. No one born there will spend a penny they haven't looked at first.
Pennywell strikes the Crown's face now, the first Reeve's own, and calls the argument settled.
Pennywell's silver runs faceless out of the Free Companies' chest now, weighed, never counted.
Pennywell strikes the old king's face now, and no one who spends it looks at it twice before it's gone.
An Envoy talked the Crown's warden and the Companies' paymaster into signing the same coin. Neither has stopped watching the other since.
Robin still hears hammers on quarter-days. She says it sounds less lonely now that someone finally answered.
Robin's river penny sits in Meva's ledger of faces now, one more coin counted rather than kept.
Robin kept her penny unread. She still won't say what she thinks it means, only that it's hers.
Dray's chest crossed the ford at dusk and reached the far bank whole, drowned moneyer and all.
Pennywell's ford errand bought the Free Companies' road under the pass, same as Gullhaven's fog and Hornhallow's timber did.
The Crown came back for Pennywell's vault after all. What it found waiting there depended on who'd been asked to pay for keeping it shut.
The struck penny's dies stand in their own niche at Pennywell's vault-door now, for anyone who doubts the rite to go and see.
The dies that struck the king's penny at Pennywell's door now rest at the Keepers' Hall, proof a rite was carried whole.
Pennywell's melted hoard went to the Regent's coffers in the end, counted, weighed, and gone.
Pennywell's melted hoard stayed at the Ironbound's furnace, and the hold's own tools have run sharper since.
A Warden got a straight answer out of Sergeant Wray at Pennywell's stair, watch to watch, that nobody else was offered.
